summary:
Turn 4 delivered a sourced correction of the active Candidate's premise plus a map-level resolution of the recovery dead code; no requirement, premise or history was weakened.

Correction (important). Re-reading handlePreAcceptReply showed the fast path does not publish the leader's own proposal vector: mergeAttributes' componentwise maximum of (seq, deps) is written back into the leader bookkeeping (lb.deps/lb.seq = merged while lb.status <= PREACCEPTED_EQ) before the branch is chosen, and both the fast-commit branch and the accept branch then copy that merged vector into the instance. So the N<=3 with Thrifty exemption does not decide which vector is committed; it removes the requirement that every counted reply already equals the merged vector, which is the step that otherwise either certifies agreement or triggers the accept round that puts the merged vector on a majority. The exposure is now stated precisely instead of incorrectly: the leader's record keeps the proposal ballot as vbal (startPhase1 sets bal and vbal; the fast-commit branch sets bal only) while a pre-accepting peer records the same pre-accept ballot, so a recovery that keeps the reply with the highest vbal (element.VBallot >= lb.ballot, last-wins iteration) cannot prefer the committed merged vector over a strictly smaller one held by a peer. The Candidate's unknowns were revised to that discriminator, including handleCommit's early return for Status >= COMMITTED, which can freeze the vector a replica already holds.

Frontier cleanup. Sub-cases 3 and 4 of handlePrepareReply carry textually identical guards, so sub-case 3 always wins and sub-case 4 never runs; because bcastTryPreAccept is called only from sub-case 4, the whole TryPreAccept path (handleTryPreAccept, findPreAcceptConflicts, handleTryPreAcceptReply, possibleQuorum, deferMap) is unreachable dead code. The possibleQuorum[tpar.AcceptorId] counting error therefore has no reachable consequence, and a recovery with weaker pre-accept support falls to sub-case 5, which restarts phase 1 with the recovered value, a more conservative path.

Map updates (same product, accepted base version 2). B4 gained the merge-installation guard and the sharpened unknown; B11 and B12 had their open unknowns replaced by the sourced unreachability results; core_overview's open details for the identical guards, the possibleQuorum counting error and the N<=3 exemption were rewritten accordingly, with map_changes entries for all four modified objects and preserves explanations for the unchanged requirements, dependencies and observation scope.
